11: ## 1. Executive Summary & Architectural Overview
12: 
13: Phase 3 of OpenFlightReader delivers the export, visualization, and application layer on top of `flightreader-core`. The core engine (`flightreader-core`, delivered in Phases 1 and 2) produces asynchronous, strongly-typed telemetry records:
14: - **OSD Telemetry (Record Type 1)**: Primary navigation cadence (~10 Hz).
15: - **Home Point Telemetry (Record Type 2)**: Navigation reference & blackbox index (~1 Hz).
16: - **Gimbal Telemetry (Record Type 3)**: Attitude cadence (~10–20 Hz).
17: - **RC Sticks (Record Type 4)**: Pilot control inputs (~10–20 Hz).
18: - **Battery Suite (Record Types 6, 7, 8, 22, 50)**: Diagnostic cadence (~1–2 Hz).
19: - **Blackbox `.DAT` Frames (Payloads 0x01, 0x12, 0x0A)**: High-frequency sensor samples (50–200 Hz).
20: 
21: Because each sensor stream reports at divergent frequencies and non-coincident timestamps, exporting tabular (CSV) or geospatial (KML, GPX, GeoJSON) flight logs cannot write one row per raw record envelope. Doing so would produce sparse, incomplete rows where Battery rows lack coordinates and OSD rows lack battery metrics.
22: 
23: `crates/flightreader-export` provides the foundational aggregation and filtering pipeline that converts these divergent streams into a clean, synchronized, 10 Hz monotonic time-series (`FlightDataset`) ready for downstream export and visualization.
24: 
25: ```
26:                   Raw Binary Flight Log (.txt / .DAT)
27:                                   │
28:                                   ▼
29:                       crates/flightreader-core
30:                (RecordEnvelopeIterator / DatFrameIterator)
31:                                   │
32:                                   ▼
33:                      crates/flightreader-export
34:          ┌────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
35:          ▼                                                 ▼
36: TelemetryAggregator                                  FilterPipeline
37: - Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) forward-fill                 - Time window (--start, --end)
38: - Master clock timestamp calculation                 - Rate decimation (--rate <HZ>)
39: - Ground increment + airborne sync                   - Critical landmark event pinning
40: - Geodetic MSL (EGM2008) & AGL elevations             (Takeoff, Landing, Mode, RTH, Extrema)
41:          │                                                 │
42:          └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┘
43:                                   ▼
44:                             FlightDataset
45:                      (Metadata, Points, Events)
46:                                   │
47:               ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
48:               ▼                   ▼                   ▼
49:           CSV Export          KML Export          GPX Export
50:           (RFC 4180)          (OGC 2.2)         (TopoGrafix 1.1)
51: ```

109: ## 3. Data Model Architecture (`src/model.rs`)
110: 
111: The data model provides the unified representation consumed by all downstream exporters (CSV, KML, GPX, GeoJSON, and local server state).
112: 
113: ### 3.1 `TelemetryPoint`
114: A single synchronized time-series point capturing the aircraft's physical state at a discrete 10 Hz instant:
115: 
116: ```rust
117: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
118: 
119: /// A synchronized, multi-sensor flight telemetry point at a discrete instant.
120: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
121: pub struct TelemetryPoint {
122:     /// Monotonically increasing sequential index of this point in the dataset (0-based).
123:     pub index: usize,
124:     /// Absolute UTC Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
125:     pub timestamp_utc_ms: i64,
126:     /// ISO 8601 formatted UTC timestamp string (e.g. "2026-10-27T14:32:00.100Z").
127:     pub timestamp_iso8601: String,
128:     /// Cumulative elapsed duration in seconds since logging began (monotonically increasing).
129:     pub elapsed_s: f64,
130:     /// Official DJI airborne flight timer in seconds (0.0 during pre-takeoff ground idling).
131:     pub fly_time_s: f64,
132:

134:     /// WGS84 Geodetic Latitude in decimal degrees (-90.0 to +90.0).
135:     pub latitude: f64,
136:     /// WGS84 Geodetic Longitude in decimal degrees (-180.0 to +180.0).
137:     pub longitude: f64,
138:     /// Orthometric altitude above Mean Sea Level (MSL) in meters (via EGM2008 / Home datum).
139:     pub altitude_msl: f64,
140:     /// Relative altitude Above Ground Level (AGL) in meters relative to takeoff point.
141:     pub altitude_agl: f64,
142:     /// Raw barometric relative height from OSD in meters.
143:     pub altitude_baro: f64,
144:     /// Ultrasonic / optical flow ground clearance in meters (if sensor active).
145:     pub vps_height_m: Option<f64>,
146: 
147:     // --- Kinematics & Velocities (NED Frame) ---
148:     /// Horizontal ground speed in m/s (sqrt(vel_n^2 + vel_e^2)).
149:     pub ground_speed_mps: f64,
150:     /// 3D total speed magnitude in m/s (sqrt(vel_n^2 + vel_e^2 + vel_d^2)).
151:     pub speed_3d_mps: f64,
152:     /// Climb rate in m/s (-vel_d, positive = ascending).
153:     pub climb_rate_mps: f64,
154:     /// Velocity along North axis in m/s (NED frame).
155:     pub vel_n: f64,
156:     /// Velocity along East axis in m/s (NED frame).
157:     pub vel_e: f64,
158:     /// Velocity along Down axis in m/s (NED frame).
159:     pub vel_d: f64,
160:     /// Ground track course bearing in degrees clockwise from True North (0.0 to 360.0).
161:     pub course_deg: f64,
162: 
163:     // --- Aircraft Attitude (Euler Angles) ---
164:     /// Aircraft pitch angle in degrees (-90.0 nose down to +90.0 nose up).
165:     pub pitch_deg: f64,

391: ## 4. Stateful Zero-Order Hold Aggregator (`src/aggregator.rs`)
392: 
393: ### 4.1 Ingestion Model & State Accumulator
394: `TelemetryAggregator` ingests raw records sequentially from `RecordEnvelopeIterator` (for `.txt` files) or `DatFrameIterator` (for `.DAT` blackbox files). It maintains an internal zero-order hold state:
395: 
396: ```rust
397: pub struct TelemetryAggregator {
398:     version: u8,
399:     details_log_start_ms: i64,
400:     egm: Option<Egm2008Model>,
401: 
402:     // --- Zero-Order Hold Sensor State ---
403:     latest_osd: Option<OsdRecord>,
404:     latest_home: Option<HomeRecord>,
405:     latest_gimbal: Option<GimbalRecord>,
406:     latest_rc: Option<RcRecord>,
407:     latest_battery_summary: Option<BatteryEnergySummary>,
408:     latest_battery_cells: Option<BatteryCellVoltages>,
409:     latest_smart_battery: Option<SmartBatteryGroup>,
410:     latest_recover: Option<FlightRecordRecover>,
411: 
412:     // --- Time Tracking & Monotonicity ---
413:     point_index: usize,
414:     pre_takeoff_count: usize,
415:     takeoff_elapsed_s: Option<f64>,
416:     last_timestamp_ms: i64,
417:     last_elapsed_s: f64,
418: 
419:     // --- State Transition Detection ---
420:     prev_flight_mode: Option<FlightMode>,
421:     prev_motor_up: bool,
422:     prev_failsafe: bool,
423: 
424:     // --- Metrics Accumulation ---
425:     max_alt_agl: f64,
426:     max_alt_msl: f64,
427:     max_h_speed: f64,
428:     max_v_speed: f64,
429:     total_distance_m: f64,
430:     prev_lat: Option<f64>,
431:     prev_lon: Option<f64>,
432: 
433:     // --- Emitted Series ---
434:     points: Vec<TelemetryPoint>,
435:     events: Vec<FlightEvent>,
436: }
437: ```
438: 
439: ### 4.2 Timestamp Reconstruction & Monotonicity Algorithm
440: The aggregator resolves the critical timing challenge between pre-takeoff stationary ground logging and post-takeoff airborne logging:
441: 
442: 1. **Base Session Start (`DetailsLogStartMilliseconds`)**:
443:    - Extracted from Details block at relative offset $91..99$.
444:    - If missing or zero ($t_0 \le 0$), fall back to relative elapsed time from $0$.
445: 
446: 2. **Dual-Phase Time Reconstruction**:
447:    ```rust
448:    let (timestamp_utc_ms, elapsed_s) = if osd.fly_time_s > 0.0 {
449:        // Airborne Phase: Synchronize to official motor timer fly_time_s
450:        let elapsed = if let Some(t_takeoff) = self.takeoff_elapsed_s {
451:            t_takeoff + osd.fly_time_s
452:        } else {
453:            let t_ground = self.pre_takeoff_count as f64 * 0.1;
454:            self.takeoff_elapsed_s = Some(t_ground);
455:            t_ground + osd.fly_time_s
456:        };
457: 
458:        let ts = if self.details_log_start_ms > 0 {
459:            self.details_log_start_ms + (elapsed * 1000.0).round() as i64
460:        } else {
461:            (elapsed * 1000.0).round() as i64
462:        };
463:        (ts, elapsed)
464:    } else {
465:        // Pre-Takeoff Ground Phase: Advance in strict 100 ms increments (10 Hz cadence)
466:        let elapsed = self.pre_takeoff_count as f64 * 0.1;
467:        self.pre_takeoff_count += 1;
468: 
469:        let ts = if self.details_log_start_ms > 0 {
470:            self.details_log_start_ms + (elapsed * 1000.0).round() as i64
471:        } else {
472:            (elapsed * 1000.0).round() as i64
473:        };
474:        (ts, elapsed)
475:    };
476:    ```
477: 
478: 3. **Monotonicity Guarantee**:
479:    If an asynchronous glitch produces non-increasing timestamps, the aggregator clamps:
480:    $$t_{\text{current}} = \max(t_{\text{current}}, t_{\text{previous}} + 1\text{ ms})$$
481:    $$t_{\text{elapsed}} = \max(t_{\text{elapsed}}, t_{\text{prev\_elapsed}} + 0.001\text{ s})$$
482: 
483: ### 4.3 Vertical Elevation Calculations ($H_{\text{MSL}}$ and $H_{\text{AGL}}$)
484: - `altitude_agl = osd.height_m`: Barometric relative altitude above takeoff reference.
485: - `altitude_msl`:
486:   1. If `latest_home` is recorded:
487:      $$H_{\text{takeoff\_msl}} = \text{home.height\_m as f64}$$
488:   2. If `Egm2008Model` is configured and coordinates are valid:
489:      Calculate undulation $N = \text{egm.undulation}(\phi_{\text{osd}}, \lambda_{\text{osd}})$.
490:      Adjust takeoff elevation or GPS elevation:
491:      $$H_{\text{msl}} = H_{\text{takeoff\_msl}} + \text{osd.height\_m}$$
492:   3. Default fallback: $H_{\text{msl}} = \text{osd.height\_m}$.
493: 
494: ### 4.4 Automated Landmark Event Detection
495: During `process_envelope`, the aggregator monitors state transitions:
496: 1. **Takeoff**: `osd.fly_state.is_motor_up() && !self.prev_motor_up`
497:    - Emits `FlightEventType::Takeoff`.
498:    - Records `takeoff_elapsed_s`.
499: 2. **Landing**: `!osd.fly_state.is_motor_up() && self.prev_motor_up && self.takeoff_elapsed_s.is_some()`
500:    - Emits `FlightEventType::Landing`.
501: 3. **Flight Mode Transition**: `osd.flight_status.flyc_state() != self.prev_flight_mode`
502:    - Emits `FlightEventType::FlightModeChange { from, to }`.
503: 4. **Failsafe Engagement**: `osd.flight_status.is_failsafe_active() && !self.prev_failsafe`
504:    - Emits `FlightEventType::RthTriggered`.
505: 5. **Home Point Locked**: When `HomeRecord` is received with `status.is_home_record() == true`.
506:    - Emits `FlightEventType::HomeRecorded`.

510: ## 5. Filtering & Decimation Engine (`src/filter.rs`)
511: 
512: ### 5.1 Time Window Filtering (`--start`, `--end`)
513: 
514: #### 1. Supported Formats
515: The filter parses flexible user-supplied boundaries:
516: - **Elapsed Seconds**: `"30.5"`, `"120"` -> `TimeBound::ElapsedSeconds(f64)`.
517: - **Clock Notation**:
518:   - `"01:30"` -> $1 \times 60 + 30 = 90.0\text{ seconds}$.
519:   - `"01:15:30"` -> $1 \times 3600 + 15 \times 60 + 30 = 4530.0\text{ seconds}$.
520: - **ISO 8601 UTC Timestamps**:
521:   - `"2026-10-27T14:33:00Z"` -> `TimeBound::UtcEpochMs(i64)`.
522: 
523: #### 2. Data Structures
524: ```rust
525: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
526: pub enum TimeBound {
527:     ElapsedSeconds(f64),
528:     UtcEpochMs(i64),
529: }
530: 
531: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Default)]
532: pub struct TimeFilter {
533:     pub start: Option<TimeBound>,
534:     pub end: Option<TimeBound>,
535: }
536: ```
537: 
538: #### 3. Boundary Validation & Edge Cases
539: - **Validation**:
540:   - If both `start` and `end` are `ElapsedSeconds`: requires $t_{\text{start}} \le t_{\text{end}}$. If $t_{\text{start}} > t_{\text{end}}$, return `Err(ExportError::InvalidTimeWindow)`.
541:   - If both are `UtcEpochMs`: requires $t_{\text{start}} \le t_{\text{end}}$.
542:   - If mixed: compare during point matching using the dataset's base `start_time_utc_ms`.
543: - **Edge Cases**:
544:   - $t_{\text{start}} \ge \text{Duration}$: Valid query resulting in an empty points slice (`Vec::new()`), emitting a warning rather than panicking.
545:   - $t_{\text{end}} > \text{Duration}$: Clamped to the end of the dataset.
546:   - Half-open / inclusive semantics: Inclusive interval $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$.
547: 
548: ### 5.2 Decimation Engine (`--rate <HZ>`) with Landmark Event Pinning
549: 
550: #### 1. Uniform Time-Binning Decimation
551: High-rate flight streams (10 Hz .txt, 50–200 Hz .DAT) create multi-megabyte exports. `--rate <HZ>` downsamples the stream to target frequency $R$:
552: - Target bin duration: $\Delta t = \frac{1.0}{R}\text{ seconds}$.
553: - Bins partition elapsed time: $I_k = [k \Delta t, (k+1) \Delta t)$.
554: - In each bin without pinned landmarks, select the point minimizing $|t_i - (k + 0.5)\Delta t|$.
555: 
556: #### 2. Critical Landmark Pinning Algorithm
557: Decimation must NEVER drop safety-critical or mission-defining single-frame events. The decimator pre-identifies a set of `pinned_indices`:
558: ```rust
559: let mut pinned = HashSet::new();
560: 
561: if !points.is_empty() {
562:     pinned.insert(0);                  // Dataset start
563:     pinned.insert(points.len() - 1);  // Dataset end
564: }
565: 
566: // 1. Takeoff Point
567: if let Some(takeoff_idx) = points.iter().position(|p| p.is_motor_on) {
568:     pinned.insert(takeoff_idx);
569: }
570: 
571: // 2. Landing Point
572: if let Some(landing_idx) = points.iter().rposition(|p| p.is_motor_on) {
573:     if landing_idx + 1 < points.len() {
574:         pinned.insert(landing_idx + 1); // Disarm instant
575:     } else {
576:         pinned.insert(landing_idx);
577:     }
578: }
579: 
580: // 3. Flight Mode Transitions
581: for i in 1..points.len() {
582:     if points[i].flight_mode != points[i - 1].flight_mode {
583:         pinned.insert(i);
584:     }
585: }
586: 
587: // 4. Return-To-Home Failsafe Activations
588: for i in 1..points.len() {
589:     if points[i].is_failsafe_active && !points[i - 1].is_failsafe_active {
590:         pinned.insert(i);
591:     }
592: }
593: 
594: // 5. Safety Alerts & Warnings
595: for (i, p) in points.iter().enumerate() {
596:     if p.app_warning.is_some() {
597:         pinned.insert(i);
598:     }
599: }
600: 
601: // 6. Max Altitude & Max Speed Extrema
602: let mut max_alt_idx = 0;
603: let mut max_spd_idx = 0;
604: let mut max_alt = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
605: let mut max_spd = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
606: 
607: for (i, p) in points.iter().enumerate() {
608:     if p.altitude_msl > max_alt {
609:         max_alt = p.altitude_msl;
610:         max_alt_idx = i;
611:     }
612:     if p.ground_speed_mps > max_spd {
613:         max_spd = p.ground_speed_mps;
614:         max_spd_idx = i;
615:     }
616: }
617: if !points.is_empty() {
618:     pinned.insert(max_alt_idx);
619:     pinned.insert(max_spd_idx);
620: }
621: ```
622: 
623: #### 3. Bin Fusion Logic
624: For each time bin $I_k$:
625: - If one or more `pinned` indices fall in $I_k$: **all pinned indices are retained**.
626: - If no pinned index falls in $I_k$: the candidate point closest to bin center is retained.
627: - The resulting indices are sorted and deduplicated:
628:   $$\text{output\_points} = \text{indices}.\text{into\_iter}().\text{map}(|i|\ \text{points}[i].\text{clone}()).\text{collect}()$$
629: 
630: This guarantees:
631: 1. Zero loss of critical events regardless of aggressive decimation (e.g. `--rate 0.1` still preserves takeoff, mode switches, RTH triggers, and peak altitude).
632: 2. Monotonic time ordering without phase shift or time drift.

63: ## 1. Executive Summary
64: 
65: Phase 3 Milestone M1 of OpenFlightReader establishes `crates/flightreader-export`, the high-performance serialization tier converting synchronized telemetry records produced by `flightreader-core` into standard geospatial, tabular, and analytical file formats.
66: 
67: This report specifies the concrete architecture, algorithms, data structures, and implementation blueprints for all five exporter engines and the unifying exporter trait:
68: 1. **`FlightExporter` Trait (`mod.rs`)**: A generic, zero-allocation streaming export interface decoupled from concrete storage media, operating over arbitrary `std::io::Write` sinks.
69: 2. **RFC 4180 CSV Exporter (`csv.rs`)**: High-precision tabular time-series serialization with four synchronized time columns, 8-decimal-place geodetic coordinates ($1.1\text{ mm}$ spatial resolution), MSL/AGL vertical datums, NED velocities, attitude Euler angles, RC stick deflections, battery cell matrices, and Telemetry Overlay dialect support.
70: 3. **OGC KML 2.2 Exporter (`kml.rs`)**: 3D extruded flight trajectory path with `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`, color-coded multi-segment placemarks with shared boundary vertices, 2D clamped ground track, and custom placemark waypoints.
71: 4. **TopoGrafix GPX 1.1 Exporter (`gpx.rs`)**: GNSS exchange format containing standard trackpoints with WGS84 elevation, ISO 8601 UTC timestamps, kinematic tags, and extended `<uav:telemetry>` attributes.
72: 5. **RFC 7946 GeoJSON Exporter (`geojson.rs`)**: 3D `LineString` feature collections with WGS84 CRS84 datum, 3D bounding boxes, landmark point features, and optional columnar coordinate properties.
73: 6. **Flight Summary JSON Exporter (`json.rs`)**: Hierarchical, non-spatial JSON digest capturing vehicle serial numbers, flight duration, kinematic extremes, battery health metrics, and significant event logs.
74: 
75: All exporter components strictly adhere to `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, use streaming buffered I/O, enforce invariant culture numeric formatting (period `.` decimal separator), and provide graceful fallback handling for empty or degenerate flight datasets.

79: ## 2. Module Architecture & The `FlightExporter` Trait (`src/exporters/mod.rs`)
80: 
81: ### 2.1 Trait Definition & Design Rationale
82: 
83: The central abstraction of `crates/flightreader-export` is the `FlightExporter` trait. It decouples the data aggregation model (`FlightDataset`) from file systems, network streams, or memory buffers:
84: 
85: ```rust
86: pub trait FlightExporter {
87:     /// Export the dataset to the provided writer.
88:     fn export<W: std::io::Write>(
89:         &self,
90:         dataset: &FlightDataset,
91:         writer: &mut W,
92:     ) -> Result<(), ExportError>;
93: }
94: ```
95: 
96: #### Key Design Invariants:
97: 1. **Generic Over `W: std::io::Write`**: Allows direct streaming to `std::fs::File`, `std::io::BufWriter`, `Vec<u8>`, network sockets, or hashing wrappers without creating intermediate multi-megabyte string allocations.
98: 2. **Immutable `&self` and `&FlightDataset`**: Exporters do not mutate the dataset. Exporter instances can be reused across multiple flights and shared across threads (`Send + Sync`).
99: 3. **Structured Error Handling**: Returns `Result<(), ExportError>`, avoiding panics on I/O failures or invalid inputs.
100: 
101: ### 2.2 Ergonomic Extension Methods (`FlightExporterExt`)
102: 
103: To streamline developer experience in CLI and tests, an extension trait provides helper methods automatically implemented for all types implementing `FlightExporter`:
104: 
105: ```rust
106: pub trait FlightExporterExt: FlightExporter {
107:     /// Export the dataset directly to a file on disk with buffered I/O.
108:     fn export_to_file<P: AsRef<std::path::Path>>(
109:         &self,
110:         dataset: &FlightDataset,
111:         path: P,
112:     ) -> Result<(), ExportError> {
113:         let file = std::fs::File::create(path)?;
114:         let mut writer = std::io::BufWriter::new(file);
115:         self.export(dataset, &mut writer)?;
116:         writer.flush()?;
117:         Ok(())
118:     }
119: 
120:     /// Export the dataset into a memory buffer (`Vec<u8>`).
121:     fn export_to_vec(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ExportError> {
122:         let mut buf = Vec::new();
123:         self.export(dataset, &mut buf)?;
124:         Ok(buf)
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Export the dataset into a UTF-8 string.
128:     fn export_to_string(&self, dataset: &FlightDataset) -> Result<String, ExportError> {
129:         let bytes = self.export_to_vec(dataset)?;
130:         String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|e| ExportError::Formatting(e.to_string()))
131:     }
132: }
133: 
134: impl<T: FlightExporter + ?Sized> FlightExporterExt for T {}
135: ```

237: ## 3. RFC 4180 CSV Telemetry Exporter (`src/exporters/csv.rs`)
238: 
239: ### 3.1 Standards Compliance (CRLF, Escaping, Invariant Culture)
240: 
241: The CSV exporter strictly complies with IETF RFC 4180:
242: 1. **Line Terminators**: Default to strict CRLF (`\r\n`, ASCII `0x0D 0x0A`). Configurable to Unix LF (`\n`) via `CsvOptions`.
243: 2. **Field Delimiters**: ASCII comma (`,`, `0x2C`).
244: 3. **Escaping**: If a text value contains a comma (`,`), double quote (`"`), carriage return (`\r`), or newline (`\n`), the entire field is enclosed in double quotes. Any internal quote is escaped by doubling it (`""`).
245:    $$\text{"High Wind, Landing"} \longrightarrow \text{"\"High Wind, Landing\""}$$
246:    $$\text{Pilot said "Caution"} \longrightarrow \text{"\"Pilot said \"\"Caution\"\"\""}$$
247: 4. **Invariant Culture**: Floating-point values are formatted strictly with period `.` as decimal separator regardless of host OS locale. Thousands grouping commas are strictly prohibited.
248: 5. **Byte Order Mark (BOM)**: Configurable optional UTF-8 BOM (`0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF`) to ensure Microsoft Excel opens UTF-8 strings cleanly without garbling non-ASCII characters.

303: ### 3.3 Telemetry Overlay Dialect (Juan Irache GoPro Format)
304: 
305: When configured with `CsvDialect::TelemetryOverlay`, the exporter emits the exact header and column set expected by Juan Irache's Telemetry Overlay tool:
306: - **Header**: `utc,lat,lon,alt,speed2d,speed3d,pitch,roll,yaw,heading,distance,battery,satellites,flightMode`
307: - **Units**:
308:   - `utc`: ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`2026-10-28T05:30:00.100Z`).
309:   - `lat`, `lon`: Decimal degrees (8 decimal places).
310:   - `alt`: MSL orthometric altitude in meters (`{:.2}`).
311:   - `speed2d`: Horizontal ground speed in m/s (`{:.2}`).
312:   - `speed3d`: 3D velocity magnitude in m/s (`{:.2}`).
313:   - `pitch`, `roll`, `yaw`: Attitude degrees (`{:.1}`).
314:   - `heading`: Compass heading in $[0.0, 360.0)^\circ$ (`{:.1}`).
315:   - `distance`: Distance to home in meters (`{:.2}`).
316:   - `battery`: SoC percentage ($0 \dots 100$).
317:   - `satellites`: Locked GNSS satellites count.
318:   - `flightMode`: Escaped flight mode string.
319: 
320: ### 3.4 Implementation Architecture & Buffer Management
321: 
322: ```rust
323: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
324: pub enum CsvDialect {
325:     #[default]
326:     Standard,
327:     TelemetryOverlay,
328: }
329: 
330: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
331: pub enum LineEnding {
332:     #[default]
333:     Crlf,
334:     Lf,
335: }
336: 
337: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
338: pub struct CsvOptions {
339:     pub dialect: CsvDialect,
340:     pub include_bom: bool,
341:     pub line_ending: LineEnding,
342: }
343: 
344: impl Default for CsvOptions {
345:     fn default() -> Self {
346:         Self {
347:             dialect: CsvDialect::Standard,
348:             include_bom: false,
349:             line_ending: LineEnding::Crlf,
350:         }
351:     }
352: }
353: ```
354: 
355: The exporter uses a reusable `String` scratchpad to format each row and flush directly into the writer, keeping memory allocations to a constant $O(1)$ regardless of flight duration.

359: ## 4. OGC KML 2.2 3D Extruded Trajectory Exporter (`src/exporters/kml.rs`)
360: 
361: ### 4.1 OGC 07-147r2 Standards, Namespaces & XML Prolog
362: 
363: The KML exporter generates valid XML complying with OGC KML 2.2 (OGC 07-147r2 / ISO/IEC 19772:2011):
364: - XML 1.0 Declaration: `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`
365: - Root Element: `<kml xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2">`
366: - Child Elements in Strict Schema Order: `<Document>` $\to$ `<Style>` / `<StyleMap>` $\to$ `<Placemark>` $\to$ `<LineString>` / `<Point>`.
367: 
368: ### 4.2 Style Palette & `AABBGGRR` Hex Color Encoding
369: 
370: KML standardizes colors in **hexadecimal ABGR order** (`aabbggrr`):
371: $$\text{KML Hex} = \text{Alpha (2 hex)} + \text{Blue (2 hex)} + \text{Green (2 hex)} + \text{Red (2 hex)}$$
372: 
373: #### Mathematical Conversion Function
374: Given a standard Web RGB hex string `#RRGGBB` and opacity percentage $\alpha\% \in [0, 100]$:
375: 1. $A = \lfloor \alpha \times 2.55 \rfloor$
376: 2. Extract $R, G, B$ bytes.
377: 3. $\text{Color}_{\text{KML}} = \text{format!("{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}", A, B, G, R)}$
378: 
379: #### Four Authoritative Styles (from `TemplateLog.kml`):
380: 1. **`LineStyleNormal`** (Green cruise):
381:    - `<LineStyle><color>ff00ff00</color><width>3</width></LineStyle>`
382:    - `<PolyStyle><color>7f00ff00</color><fill>1</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`
383: 2. **`LineStyleWarning`** (Orange cautionary):
384:    - `<LineStyle><color>ff00a5ff</color><width>3</width></LineStyle>`
385:    - `<PolyStyle><color>7f00a5ff</color><fill>1</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`
386: 3. **`LineStyleError`** (Red alert / RTH):
387:    - `<LineStyle><color>ff0000ff</color><width>4</width></LineStyle>`
388:    - `<PolyStyle><color>7f0000ff</color><fill>1</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`
389: 4. **`LineStyleGroundTrack`** (Translucent gray 2D ground footprint):
390:    - `<LineStyle><color>7f333333</color><width>1</width></LineStyle>`
391:    - `<PolyStyle><fill>0</fill><outline>0</outline></PolyStyle>`
392: 
393: Placemark styles include `NormalPlacemark`, `HiddenPlacemark`, and a `<StyleMap id="ShowHidePlacemark">` pairing mouse-hover states.
394: 
395: ### 4.3 3D Flight Path Geometry (`<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`)
396: 
397: 1. **Coordinate Tuple Order**:
398:    In KML, coordinates are defined strictly as:
399:    $$\text{longitude},\text{latitude},\text{altitude}$$
400:    > ⚠️ **Critical Requirement**: Longitude ($-180.0 \dots +180.0$) MUST precede Latitude ($-90.0 \dots +90.0$). Reversing this flips the drone trajectory to the antipodal hemisphere!
401: 2. **Altitude Mode**:
402:    `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>` interprets the altitude coordinate as elevation above the WGS84 EGM2008 Mean Sea Level (MSL) geoid in meters ($H = h - N$). This positions the flight polyline at its actual physical height in Google Earth's 3D terrain viewer.
403: 3. **Vertical Extrusion**:
404:    `<extrude>1</extrude>` projects a vertical semi-transparent curtain from the airborne trajectory line directly down to the terrain surface. The curtain color and alpha are governed by the `<PolyStyle>` defined in the active `<Style>`. If fill transparency is configured to 100% (fully invisible), `<extrude>1</extrude>` is omitted.
405: 
406: ### 4.4 Segmented State Styling & Shared Boundary Vertices
407: 
408: When flight conditions change (e.g. from Normal flight to a High Wind Warning, or engaging Return-To-Home), the flight path splits into multiple `<Placemark>` line segments:
409: - Normal flight $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleNormal</styleUrl>`
410: - Non-critical warning $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleWarning</styleUrl>`
411: - Critical emergency / RTH failsafe $\to$ `<styleUrl>#LineStyleError</styleUrl>`
412: 
413: #### Shared Boundary Vertex Rule
414: > ⚠️ **Visual Continuity Invariant**: To prevent visual cracks/gaps between adjacent segments in Google Earth, the last coordinate tuple of segment $N$ **must be duplicated** as the first coordinate tuple of segment $N+1$:
415: $$P_{\text{segment } N, \text{last}} \equiv P_{\text{segment } N+1, \text{first}}$$
416: 
417: ### 4.5 2D Clamped Ground Track (Shadow Line)
418: 
419: To give pilots and analysts an unobstructed view of the ground trajectory independent of camera viewing angle, the KML exporter generates an auxiliary `<Placemark>`:
420: ```xml
421: <Placemark>
422:   <name>Ground Track</name>
423:   <styleUrl>#LineStyleGroundTrack</styleUrl>
424:   <LineString>
425:     <extrude>0</extrude>
426:     <altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>
427:     <coordinates>
428:       -122.33214500,47.60621200,0
429:       -122.33215600,47.60623400,0
430:     </coordinates>
431:   </LineString>
432: </Placemark>
433: ```
434: `<altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>` drapes the line directly onto Google Earth's 3D digital elevation model.
435: 
436: ### 4.6 Waypoint Placemarks (Takeoff, Home Point, RTH, Warnings)
437: 
438: The exporter inserts individual event placemarks along the flight timeline:
439: 
440: 1. **Takeoff Point Placemark**:
441:    - Location: First point where `is_motor_on == true`.
442:    - Style: Green pushpin icon (`http://maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/pal4/icon21.png`).
443:    - Description: CDATA block containing Takeoff UTC time and ground elevation.
444: 2. **Home Point Placemark**:
445:    - Location: Calibrated `HOME.latitude`, `HOME.longitude`, takeoff MSL altitude.
446:    - Style: Home icon (`http://maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/pal4/icon57.png`).
447:    - Description: CDATA block with RTH cruise height.
448: 3. **RTH Failsafe Trigger Placemark**:
449:    - Location: Exact coordinates where RTH failsafe engaged (`GoHomeStatus != Standby`).
450:    - Style: Red flag icon (`http://maps.google.com/mapfiles/kml/pal4/icon49.png`).
451:    - Description: CDATA block with battery %, distance to home, and flight duration.
452: 4. **Landing Point Placemark**:
453:    - Location: Final coordinate where motors disarm.
454: 
455: ### 4.7 3D Path Reduction & Jitter Filtering (RDP Simplification)
456: 
457: Decompiled from `KmlCompressor.cs`, stationary hovering at 10 Hz generates thousands of points within a $0.5\text{ m}$ circle, creating massive polygon thrashing in Google Earth. The KML exporter includes an optional 3D path reduction stage:
458: 1. **Jitter Filter**: Points with 3D displacement $\Delta d < 0.15\text{ m}$ from the prior emitted point are skipped during steady hover.
459: 2. **3D Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP)**: Recursively simplifies the 3D trajectory polyline to within a configurable perpendicular tolerance $\epsilon$ (default $0.45\text{ m}$), preserving flight profile fidelity while shrinking file size by $60\text{--}80\%$.

463: ## 5. TopoGrafix GPX 1.1 Trackpoint Exporter (`src/exporters/gpx.rs`)
464: 
465: ### 5.1 GPX 1.1 XML Schema & UAV Namespace Configuration
466: 
467: The GPX exporter outputs standard XML conforming to TopoGrafix GPX 1.1:
468: ```xml
469: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
470: <gpx version="1.1" creator="OpenFlightReader"
471:      xmlns="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1"
472:      xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
473:      xmlns:uav="https://openflightreader.org/schema/gpx/1.0"
474:      xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1 http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1/gpx.xsd">
475: ```
476: 
477: ### 5.2 Waypoints (`<wpt>`) for Flight Landmarks
478: 
479: Per GPX 1.1 schema rules, top-level `<wpt>` elements MUST appear before `<trk>` containers:
480: ```xml
481:   <wpt lat="47.60621200" lon="-122.33214500">
482:     <ele>125.40</ele>
483:     <time>2026-10-28T05:30:00.000Z</time>
484:     <name>Takeoff Point</name>
485:     <sym>Airport</sym>
486:   </wpt>
487:   <wpt lat="47.60621200" lon="-122.33214500">
488:     <ele>125.40</ele>
489:     <name>Home Point</name>
490:     <sym>Home</sym>
491:   </wpt>
492: ```
493: 
494: ### 5.3 Track Hierarchy (`<trk>`, `<trkseg>`, `<trkpt>`)
495: 
496: The flight path is wrapped in a `<trk>` container with `<name>` and metadata, containing one or more `<trkseg>` continuous segments:
497: ```xml
498:   <trk>
499:     <name>DJI Flight Track</name>
500:     <trkseg>
501:       <trkpt lat="47.60621200" lon="-122.33214500">
502:         <ele>125.40</ele>
503:         <time>2026-10-28T05:30:00.000Z</time>
504:         <speed>0.00</speed>
505:         <course>180.0</course>
506:         <sat>18</sat>
507:         <extensions> ... </extensions>
508:       </trkpt>
509:     </trkseg>
510:   </trk>
511: ```
512: 
513: ### 5.4 Standard Telemetry Tags (`lat`, `lon`, `<ele>`, `<time>`, `<speed>`, `<course>`, `<sat>`)
514: 
515: - `lat` / `lon`: Decimal degrees in WGS84 datum (8 decimal places).
516: - `<ele>`: MSL orthometric elevation in meters ($H$, `{:.2}`). Correctly formats negative elevations (e.g., Death Valley, Dead Sea).
517: - `<time>`: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ` (strictly ending with `Z`).
518: - `<speed>`: Horizontal ground speed in meters per second ($m/s$).
519: - `<course>`: Track bearing / heading in degrees clockwise from True North ($0.0^\circ \dots 359.9^\circ$).
520: - `<sat>`: Count of locked GNSS satellites ($0 \dots 40$).
521: 
522: ### 5.5 Dense UAS Sensor Telemetry Extensions (`<extensions><uav:telemetry>`)
523: 
524: To preserve rich drone sensor attributes that exceed standard GPX 1.1 schema tags, the exporter injects a typed `<extensions>` node inside every `<trkpt>`:
525: ```xml
526:         <extensions>
527:           <uav:telemetry>
528:             <uav:heightAgl>42.50</uav:heightAgl>
529:             <uav:verticalSpeed>-0.80</uav:verticalSpeed>
530:             <uav:pitch>12.4</uav:pitch>
531:             <uav:roll>-2.1</uav:roll>
532:             <uav:yaw>184.2</uav:yaw>
533:             <uav:batteryPercent>84</uav:batteryPercent>
534:             <uav:batteryVoltage>15.620</uav:batteryVoltage>
535:             <uav:batteryCurrent>8.45</uav:batteryCurrent>
536:             <uav:batteryTemp>28.5</uav:batteryTemp>
537:             <uav:flightMode>P-GPS</uav:flightMode>
538:             <uav:rcThrottle>24</uav:rcThrottle>
539:             <uav:rcElevator>52</uav:rcElevator>
540:             <uav:rcAileron>0</uav:rcAileron>
541:             <uav:rcRudder>0</uav:rcRudder>
542:             <uav:homeDistance>142.80</uav:homeDistance>
543:           </uav:telemetry>
544:         </extensions>
545: ```
546: Third-party GPX viewers (Garmin BaseCamp, Strava, QGIS) ignore unknown extension namespaces while consuming standard positional tags without schema validation errors.
547: 
548: ### 5.6 Segment Splitting on Recording Gaps
549: 
550: If consecutive telemetry points exhibit a time discontinuity $> 5.0\text{ seconds}$ (radio link blackout) or if propulsion motors disarm and re-arm, the exporter terminates the current `<trkseg>` and begins a new `<trkseg>`.

554: ## 6. RFC 7946 GeoJSON Exporter (`src/exporters/geojson.rs`)
555: 
556: ### 6.1 GeoJSON Specification & WGS84 CRS84 Datum Enforcement
557: 
558: The GeoJSON exporter produces valid JSON conforming to IETF RFC 7946:
559: 1. **Coordinate Reference System**: RFC 7946 § 4 strictly mandates WGS84 with coordinate order:
560:    $$\mathbf{p} = [\text{longitude}, \text{latitude}, \text{altitude}]$$
561: 2. **Deprecation of `crs` Member**: The prior GeoJSON draft specification allowed custom `crs` members. RFC 7946 explicitly deprecates `crs`; no `crs` attribute is emitted.
562: 3. **No NaN or Infinities**: Floating point values must be valid JSON numbers ($-\infty, +\infty, \text{NaN}$ are illegal in RFC 8259 JSON and are replaced with `0.0` or `null`).
563: 
564: ### 6.2 3D Trajectory Feature (`LineString` `[lon, lat, alt]`)
565: 
566: The primary feature in the collection is the continuous 3D flight trajectory:
567: ```json
568: {
569:   "type": "Feature",
570:   "id": "flight-trajectory",
571:   "geometry": {
572:     "type": "LineString",
573:     "coordinates": [
574:       [-122.33214500, 47.60621200, 125.40],
575:       [-122.33215600, 47.60623400, 126.80],
576:       [-122.33217800, 47.60626700, 128.50]
577:     ]
578:   },
579:   "properties": {
580:     "name": "Flight Trajectory",
581:     "altitudeMode": "absolute",
582:     "startTime": "2026-10-28T05:30:00.000Z",
583:     "endTime": "2026-10-28T05:43:23.000Z",
584:     "durationSeconds": 803.0,
585:     "distanceMeters": 2450.5,
586:     "maxAltitudeAglMeters": 98.4,
587:     "maxAltitudeMslMeters": 223.8,
588:     "maxSpeedMps": 14.8
589:   }
590: }
591: ```
592: 
593: ### 6.3 Point Landmarks (Takeoff, Home, RTH, Landing)
594: 
595: Auxiliary `Point` features represent key flight events:
596: - **Takeoff Point**: `coordinates: [lon, lat, alt]`, `properties: { "name": "Takeoff Point", "timestamp": "...", "elevationMsl": ... }`
597: - **Home Point**: `coordinates: [lon, lat, alt]`, `properties: { "name": "Home Point", "rthAltitude": ... }`
598: - **RTH Event**: `coordinates: [lon, lat, alt]`, `properties: { "name": "RTH Triggered", "battery": 20, "flightTime": 750.2 }`
599: - **Landing Point**: Final touchdown location.
600: 
601: ### 6.4 3D Bounding Box Computation (`bbox`)
602: 
603: Per RFC 7946 § 5, the top-level `FeatureCollection` includes a 6-element 3D bounding box array:
604: $$\text{bbox} = [\min(\lambda), \min(\phi), \min(H), \max(\lambda), \max(\phi), \max(H)]$$
605: 
606: ```json
607: {
608:   "type": "FeatureCollection",
609:   "bbox": [-122.33500000, 47.60500000, 120.00, -122.33000000, 47.60900000, 225.00],
610:   "features": [ ... ]
611: }
612: ```
613: 
614: ### 6.5 Extended Coordinate Properties for Web Map Scrubbing
615: 
616: When `GeoJsonOptions::include_coordinate_properties` is enabled, an accompanying `coordinateProperties` object is emitted inside the `LineString` properties. This provides synchronized arrays matching the coordinates index for high-performance map scrubbing in Leaflet / MapLibre GL without fetching separate telemetry streams:
617: ```json
618: "coordinateProperties": {
619:   "times": [0.0, 0.1, 0.2],
620:   "speeds": [0.0, 1.2, 2.5],
621:   "altitudesAgl": [0.0, 1.4, 3.1],
622:   "batteryPercents": [98, 98, 97],
623:   "pitches": [0.0, 4.2, 8.5],
624:   "rolls": [0.0, -0.5, -1.2],
625:   "yaws": [180.0, 182.1, 184.2]
626: }
627: ```

717: ### 7.2 Session, Kinematic, Battery & Geographic Aggregations
718: 
719: The summary exporter iterates through the `FlightDataset` once in $O(N)$ time to compute:
720: - `totalDistanceMeters`: Cumulative geodesic distance summing haversine deltas between consecutive valid coordinates:
721:   $$d_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N-1} \text{geodesic\_distance}(\phi_i, \lambda_i, \phi_{i+1}, \lambda_{i+1})$$
722: - `maxAltitudeAglMeters`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{altitude\_agl})$.
723: - `maxAltitudeMslMeters`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{altitude\_msl})$.
724: - `maxHorizontalSpeedMps`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{ground\_speed\_mps})$.
725: - `maxVerticalSpeedMps`: $\max_i(-\text{point}_i.\text{vel\_d})$ when positive.
726: - `maxDescentSpeedMps`: $\max_i(\text{point}_i.\text{vel\_d})$ when positive.
727: - `minVoltageV`: $\min_i(\text{point}_i.\text{battery\_voltage\_mv}) \div 1000.0$.
728: - `maxCellDeviationMv`: $\max_i(\max(\text{cells}_i) - \min(\text{cells}_i))$.

41: ## 1. Executive Summary & Scope
42: 
43: Milestone M1 delivers the telemetry aggregation and multi-format geospatial export engine (`crates/flightreader-export`). To ensure high reliability, GIS interoperability, and offline compliance, all generated export artifacts must undergo rigorous schema verification against formal international standards:
44: 
45: 1. **OGC KML 2.2**: Validated for XML 1.0 well-formedness, default OGC namespace `http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2`, strict `lon,lat,alt` coordinate tuple ordering, `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`, 3D vertical path extrusion `<extrude>1</extrude>`, hex `aabbggrr` color encoding, and waypoint placemark templates.
46: 2. **TopoGrafix GPX 1.1**: Validated for GPX 1.1 schema compliance (`http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1`), trackpoint `<trkpt>` latitude and longitude bounds, ISO 8601 UTC timestamp formatting (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`), elevation `<ele>`, and UAS extension schemas (`<extensions><uav:telemetry>`).
47: 3. **RFC 4180 CSV**: Validated for strict CRLF (`\r\n`) line terminations, comma delimiters, quotation escaping (`""`), invariant numerical culture (period `.` decimal point), 8-decimal coordinate precision ($1.1\text{ mm}$ equator resolution), and column header matching.
48: 4. **RFC 7946 GeoJSON & Summary JSON**: Validated against RFC 7946 `FeatureCollection` schema, WGS84 CRS84 datum, 3D `LineString` coordinates `[lon, lat, alt]`, bounding box calculations, and hierarchical flight summary structure.
49: 
50: This document defines the schema verification strategies, test harness design, concrete test suites in `crates/flightreader-export/tests/`, and acceptance verification commands required for Milestone 1 completion.
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. Authoritative Standards & Schema Requirements
55: 
56: ### 2.1 OGC KML 2.2 Specification (OGC 07-147r2 / ISO/IEC 19772:2011)
57: 
58: #### XML Structure & Namespace Invariants
59: - **Prolog**: `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`
60: - **Root Element**: `<kml xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2">` (optional Google extensions: `xmlns:gx="http://www.google.com/kml/ext/2.2"`).
61: - **Tag Hierarchy**:
62:   ```xml
63:   <kml xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/kml/2.2">
64:     <Document>
65:       <name>...</name>
66:       <Style id="..."> ... </Style>
67:       <Placemark>
68:         <name>...</name>
69:         <styleUrl>#...</styleUrl>
70:         <LineString>
71:           <extrude>1</extrude>
72:           <tessellate>1</tessellate>
73:           <altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>
74:           <coordinates>
75:             lon,lat,alt lon,lat,alt ...
76:           </coordinates>
77:         </LineString>
78:       </Placemark>
79:     </Document>
80:   </kml>
81:   ```
82: - **Coordinate Tuple Ordering (Critical § 10.7)**:
83:   - Format: `longitude,latitude,altitude`
84:   - Longitude: Decimal degrees $[-180.0, +180.0]$.
85:   - Latitude: Decimal degrees $[-90.0, +90.0]$.
86:   - Altitude: Orthometric height in meters ($H$, MSL datum).
87:   - Delimiters: Comma (`,`) strictly between tuple components without whitespace. Whitespace, tabs, or newlines between consecutive tuples.
88: - **Altitude Modes**:
89:   - `<altitudeMode>absolute</altitudeMode>`: Required for 3D aerial trajectories (MSL datum).
90:   - `<altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>`: Required for 2D ground track footprints.
91: - **Color Format**:
92:   - Hexadecimal 8-character string formatted in **ABGR order** (`aabbggrr`):
93:     `Alpha (2 hex) + Blue (2 hex) + Green (2 hex) + Red (2 hex)`.
94: - **Styling Palettes**:
95:   - Normal cruise: `#LineStyleNormal` (`ff00ff00` line, `7f00ff00` poly).
96:   - Caution / Wind / Limit: `#LineStyleWarning` (`ff00a5ff` line, `7f00a5ff` poly).
97:   - Low Battery / RTH / Motor Error: `#LineStyleError` (`ff0000ff` line, `7f0000ff` poly).
98:   - Ground Track: `#LineStyleGroundTrack` (`7f333333` line, clampToGround).
99: 
100: ### 2.2 TopoGrafix GPX 1.1 Specification
101: 
102: #### XML Structure & Namespace Invariants
103: - **Root Element**:
104:   ```xml
105:   <gpx version="1.1" creator="OpenFlightReader"
106:        xmlns="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1"
107:        xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
108:        xmlns:uav="https://openflightreader.org/schema/gpx/1.0"
109:        xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1 http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1/gpx.xsd">
110:   ```
111: - **Track Hierarchy**: `<gpx>` $\rightarrow$ `<trk>` $\rightarrow$ `<trkseg>` $\rightarrow$ `<trkpt lat="..." lon="...">`.
112: - **Waypoint Hierarchy**: `<wpt lat="..." lon="...">` elements representing Takeoff Point, Home Point, and RTH events must precede `<trk>` elements per GPX 1.1 XSD schema ordering.
113: - **Trackpoint Invariants**:
114:   - Attributes: `lat` (latitude $[-90.0, +90.0]$), `lon` (longitude $[-180.0, +180.0]$), 8 decimal places.
115:   - `<ele>`: Absolute orthometric elevation in meters (signed float; supports below-sea-level locations).
116:   - `<time>`: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp formatted strictly as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`. Non-Z or localized timestamps violate GPX 1.1 schema validation.
117:   - `<sat>`: Integer satellite count ($0 \dots 40$).
118:   - `<extensions>`: Custom `<uav:telemetry>` element containing drone-specific channels: `heightAgl`, `verticalSpeed`, `pitch`, `roll`, `yaw`, `batteryPercent`, `batteryVoltage`, `flightMode`, `rcThrottle`, `rcElevator`, `rcAileron`, `rcRudder`, `homeDistance`.
119: 
120: ### 2.3 IETF RFC 4180 CSV Specification
121: 
122: #### Strict Grammar & Invariants
123: - **Line Endings (§ 2.1)**: Every record MUST terminate with CRLF (`\r\n`, bytes `0x0D, 0x0A`).
124: - **Delimiter**: ASCII comma (`,`, byte `0x2C`).
125: - **Header Line (§ 2.3)**: Row 0 MUST be the column names; field count must match every subsequent data row exactly (zero jagged rows).
126: - **Quoting (§ 2.5–2.7)**: Any field containing a comma, double-quote, or newline MUST be enclosed in double quotes (`"..."`). An embedded double quote MUST be escaped as two consecutive double quotes (`""`).
127: - **Culture Invariance**: Numerical formatting MUST use period (`.`) as the decimal mark; comma as decimal separator is strictly forbidden.
128: - **Coordinates & Time**:
129:   - `OSD.latitude [deg]` and `OSD.longitude [deg]` formatted to 8 decimal places.
130:   - Time columns: `Time(millisecond)` (integer), `DateTime(UTC)` (ISO 8601 `Z`), `DateTime(Local)` (formatted local), `OSD.flyTime [s]` (scaled decimal).
131: 
132: ### 2.4 IETF RFC 7946 GeoJSON & Flight Summary JSON Specification
133: 
134: #### GeoJSON Invariants (RFC 7946)
135: - **Top-Level Type**: Must be `"FeatureCollection"`.
136: - **Coordinate Reference System (§ 4)**: Strictly WGS84 CRS84. Specifying the legacy GeoJSON 2008 `"crs"` property is prohibited.
137: - **Coordinate Ordering (§ 3.1.1)**: `[longitude, latitude, altitude]` (`[easting, northing, altitude]`).
138: - **3D LineString Geometry**:
139:   ```json
140:   {
141:     "type": "Feature",
142:     "id": "flight-trajectory",
143:     "geometry": {
144:       "type": "LineString",
145:       "coordinates": [
146:         [-122.33214500, 47.60621200, 125.40],
147:         [-122.33215600, 47.60623400, 126.80]
148:       ]
149:     },
150:     "properties": { ... }
151:   }
152:   ```
153: - **Bounding Box (`bbox`)**: 6-element array `[minLon, minLat, minAlt, maxLon, maxLat, maxAlt]` enveloping all trajectory and landmark vertices.
154: - **Landmark Points**: Point features for `takeoff-point`, `home-point`, `rth-event`, `landing-point`.
155: 
156: #### Flight Summary JSON Invariants
157: - Top-level schema object containing: `$schema`, `version`, `metadata` (model, serials, software), `session` (timestamps, duration, record counts), `kinematics` (distance, max speeds, max altitudes), `battery` (SOC, min voltage, max cell spread), `geography` (takeoff, home coordinates), `events` (log of warnings and RTH triggers).
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ## 3. Schema Verification Strategy & Tooling Architecture
162: 
163: ### 3.1 In-Test Schema Validation Strategy
164: 
165: In accordance with OpenFlightReader's 100% offline, self-contained architecture, schema validation must NOT rely on external internet access or heavy native C libraries (such as `libxml2`). Instead, test suites use authoritative pure-Rust parsing engines to validate schema constraints directly within `cargo test`:
166: 
167: ```
168:                 crates/flightreader-export Exporters
169:                                 │
170:                                 ▼
171:                       Generated Byte Stream
172:                                 │
173:         ┌───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐
174:         ▼                       ▼                       ▼
175:     KML & GPX                  CSV                   GeoJSON
176:         │                       │                       │
177:         ▼                       ▼                       ▼
178:     roxmltree                  csv                 serde_json
179:   (XML 1.0 DOM &           (RFC 4180          (RFC 8259 JSON &
180:     Namespaces)          Parser & Checks)      RFC 7946 AST)
181:         │                       │                       │
182:         ▼                       ▼                       ▼
183:    Tag Hierarchy &        Equal Field Counts &   [lon, lat, alt] order &
184:    lon,lat,alt order      Escaped Quotes/CRLF    Bbox Enclosure Checks
185: ```
186: 
187: ### 3.2 Recommended Test Crates & Cargo Dependencies
188: 
189: To support thorough schema validation in `crates/flightreader-export/Cargo.toml`:
190: 
191: ```toml
192: [package]
193: name = "flightreader-export"
194: version = "0.1.0"
195: edition = "2021"
196: authors = ["OpenFlightReader Contributors"]
197: license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
198: description = "Geospatial, tabular, and time-series telemetry export engine for DJI flight records."
199: 
200: [dependencies]
201: flightreader-core = { path = "../flightreader-core" }
202: thiserror = "2.0"
203: serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
204: serde_json = "1.0"
205: chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["std", "clock"] }
206: 
207: [dev-dependencies]
208: csv = "1.3"            # RFC 4180 CSV parser & validator
209: roxmltree = "0.20"      # Strict XML 1.0 document & namespace validator
210: quick-xml = "0.37"      # High-performance event-driven XML streaming validator
211: proptest = "1.5"        # Property-based fuzzing for exporter resilience
212: tempfile = "3.17"       # Safe temporary file fixtures
213: ```
214: 
215: ### 3.3 Verification Helper Primitives
216: 
217: To eliminate repetitive test code, a shared test utility module (`tests/common/validator.rs`) provides reusable assertion helpers:
218: 
219: ```rust
220: pub struct XmlValidator;
221: impl XmlValidator {
222:     /// Validates XML 1.0 well-formedness and returns the parsed document tree.
223:     pub fn parse_xml(content: &str) -> Result<roxmltree::Document<'_>, roxmltree::Error> {
224:         roxmltree::Document::parse(content)
225:     }
226: 
227:     /// Verifies that every coordinate in a whitespace-separated KML string conforms to `lon,lat,alt`.
228:     pub fn assert_kml_coordinates_order(coords_str: &str) {
229:         for tuple in coords_str.split_whitespace() {
230:             let parts: Vec<&str> = tuple.split(',').collect();
231:             assert_eq!(parts.len(), 3, "KML coordinate tuple must have 3 components: lon,lat,alt");
232:             let lon: f64 = parts[0].parse().expect("Invalid longitude float");
233:             let lat: f64 = parts[1].parse().expect("Invalid latitude float");
234:             let _alt: f64 = parts[2].parse().expect("Invalid altitude float");
235:             assert!((-180.0..=180.0).contains(&lon), "Longitude out of bounds: {}", lon);
236:             assert!((-90.0..=90.0).contains(&lat), "Latitude out of bounds: {}", lat);
237:         }
238:     }
239: }
240: 
241: pub struct CsvValidator;
242: impl CsvValidator {
243:     /// Validates RFC 4180 parsing, CRLF line endings, and equal field counts.
244:     pub fn validate_rfc4180(bytes: &[u8]) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<Vec<String>>) {
245:         // Assert strict CRLF on each line
246:         let text = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).expect("CSV must be valid UTF-8");
247:         for line in text.split("\r\n") {
248:             assert!(!line.contains('\r'), "Stray CR character found");
249:         }
250:         let mut rdr = csv::ReaderBuilder::new()
251:             .has_headers(true)
252:             .from_reader(bytes);
253:         let headers = rdr.headers().expect("Failed to read CSV headers")
254:             .iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
255:         let mut records = Vec::new();
256:         for res in rdr.records() {
257:             let rec = res.expect("CSV row failed RFC 4180 parsing");
258:             assert_eq!(rec.len(), headers.len(), "Row length mismatch against header");
259:             records.push(rec.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect());
260:         }
261:         (headers, records)
262:     }
263: }
264: ```
265: 
266: ---
267: 
268: ## 4. Test Fixture Architecture (`tests/common/mock_data.rs`)
269: 
270: To ensure realistic, comprehensive testing across all four exporter suites, five standardized flight dataset fixtures are generated:
271: 
272: ### 4.1 Canonical Cruise Flight Dataset
273: - **Duration**: 60.0 seconds (600 points at 10 Hz).
274: - **Location**: Seattle Space Needle vicinity ($47.606212^\circ\text{ N}, -122.332145^\circ\text{ W}$).
275: - **Kinematics**: Takeoff from $125.4\text{ m MSL}$, climb to $223.8\text{ m MSL}$ ($98.4\text{ m AGL}$), cruise speed $12.5\text{ m/s}$, smooth heading turn from $0^\circ \to 90^\circ$.
276: - **Battery**: Starts at 98% ($16.4\text{ V}$), discharges to 85%, 4-cell voltage array ($4.10\text{ V} \dots 3.85\text{ V}$).
277: - **RC Sticks**: Throttle $+50\%$, Aileron $+10\%$, Rudder $0\%$, Elevator $+30\%$.
278: 
279: ### 4.2 Multi-Segment Transition Dataset
280: - **Segments**:
281:   1. Points 0..200: Cruise (`FlightMode::PGps`, Normal green style).
282:   2. Points 200..350: High Wind Warning (`APP.warning = "High Wind, Fly With Caution"`, Warning orange style).
283:   3. Points 350..500: Low Battery Critical (`APP.warning = "Low Battery 20%, RTH Initiated"`, Error red style).
284:   4. Points 500..600: Auto-Landing and Touchdown.
285: - **Verification Purpose**: Tests KML segment splitting, style transitions, and boundary vertex continuity.
286: 
287: ### 4.3 Boundary & Extremum Flight Dataset
288: - **Extreme Coordinates**: Crosses the Prime Meridian ($0.0^\circ$), Antimeridian ($180.0^\circ / -180.0^\circ$), Equator ($0.0^\circ$), and South Pole vicinity ($-89.9^\circ$).
289: - **Negative Elevations**: Flight in Death Valley / Dead Sea depressions: $-86.5\text{ m MSL}$ ($H < 0$).
290: - **Extreme Kinematics**: Supersonic/high speed test ($150\text{ m/s}$), maximum vertical climb ($25\text{ m/s}$).
291: - **Verification Purpose**: Ensures exporters never clamp negative elevations or invert coordinates near coordinate poles/boundaries.
292: 
293: ### 4.4 Special Characters & Escaping Stress Dataset
294: - Strings injected into `aircraft_name`, `flight_mode`, `APP.warning`, and `APP.tip`:
295:   - Quotes and commas: `"Caution, ""obstacle"" ahead, abort immediately!"`
296:   - XML entities: `"<Aircraft & Gimbal > 45° 'Warning' & Failsafe>"`
297:   - Unicode / Emoji / International characters: `"DJI 航模 / 飛行記録 🚁 (Mavic 3 Pro - 100% 正常)"`
298:   - Multiline warnings with embedded newlines `\n` and `\r\n`.
299: - **Verification Purpose**: Tests CSV RFC 4180 escaping, KML/GPX XML entity encoding and CDATA wrappers, and GeoJSON UTF-8 string compliance.
300: 
301: ### 4.5 Empty & Minimal Datasets
302: - **Zero-Point Dataset**: Valid `FlightMetadata` with an empty `Vec<TelemetryPoint>`.
303: - **Single-Point Dataset**: A single static point (takeoff event only).
304: - **Verification Purpose**: Validates that exporters handle edge cases gracefully without dividing by zero, panicking, or producing corrupt empty files.
305: 
306: ---
307: 
308: ## 5. Concrete Test Case Specifications
309: 
310: ### 5.1 `crates/flightreader-export/tests/csv_export_tests.rs`
311: 
312: This test suite validates RFC 4180 compliance, header matching, numeric precision, and culture invariance for CSV exports.
313: 
314: | # | Test Function Signature | Input Dataset | Expected Output / Verifications |
315: |---|---|---|---|

466: ## 8. Edge Cases
467: 
468: | # | Feature | Input | Observed Behavior |
469: |---|---|---|---|
470: | 1 | CSV Quoting | String contains comma (e.g. `APP.warning = "High Wind, Landing Soon"`) | Field enclosed in double-quotes: `"High Wind, Landing Soon"`. Unquoted commas corrupt column indexing. |
471: | 2 | CSV Quoting | String contains double quote (e.g. `APP.warning = 'Pilot said "Caution"'`) | Embedded quote escaped as double-quote: `"Pilot said ""Caution"""`. Single quotes violate RFC 4180. |
472: | 3 | CSV Decimal Separator | System locale where default decimal separator is comma `,` | Exporter enforces invariant formatting (`.`); emits `47.606212` instead of `47,606212`. |
473: | 4 | CSV Timestamp Missing | Log details start timestamp is 0 or corrupted (pre-GPS boot) | Falls back to elapsed time from zero ($t = 0.000\text{ s}$) and emits ISO UTC `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`. |
474: | 5 | CSV Battery Variants | Conflating Battery Variant A (energy summary) with Variant B (cell voltage array) | Conflating layouts shifts cell voltages by 4 bytes (2 cells), reading Cell 3 as Cell 1. Decoders must check payload length. |
475: | 6 | KML Tuple Ordering | Emitting `latitude,longitude,altitude` instead of `longitude,latitude,altitude` | Inverted coordinates flip drone path to opposite hemisphere in Google Earth. Exporter strictly writes `lon,lat,alt`. |
476: | 7 | KML Altitude Mode | Using `<altitudeMode>clampToGround</altitudeMode>` on an airborne 3D path | Flattens 3D climb and descent profiles to ground level, eliminating altitude visualization and vertical curtain walls. |
477: | 8 | KML Color Ordering | Passing standard Web hex format `#RRGGBB` directly into KML `<color>` | KML reverses RGB order to BGR (`aabbggrr`). Passing `#FF0000` (Red) naively renders as Blue in Google Earth (`ff0000` = Blue in KML). |
478: | 9 | KML Segment Gaps | Segmenting flight path by color without repeating boundary vertices | Google Earth leaves a visual gap between segment $N$ and segment $N+1$. Boundary vertex $P_{\text{split}}$ must be shared by both placemarks. |
479: | 10 | KML Coordinate Jitter | Drone hovering stationary for 10 minutes at 10 Hz (6,000 points in $0.5\text{ m}$ circle) | Jitter causes massive Google Earth polygon rendering thrashing. Must be filtered via `RemoveJitterCoords(jitterMeters = 0.15)`. |
480: | 11 | KML Extrusion Fill | `KmlLineFillTransparency` configured to 100% (fully transparent) | Omit `<extrude>1</extrude>` completely (`extrude` tag removed) to avoid rendering transparent artifacts over 3D terrain. |
481: | 12 | GPX Time Formatting | Emitting local timestamp or non-Z UTC timestamp in `<time>` | Third-party GPX viewers (Strava, Garmin BaseCamp) fail schema validation. Timestamp MUST strictly end with `Z` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`). |
482: | 13 | GPX Negative Altitude | Drone flying in below-sea-level depressions (e.g. Death Valley, Dead Sea: $-86\text{ m}$) | Elevation `<ele>` must accept signed floating-point values. Clamping to zero corrupts valid terrain data. |
483: | 14 | GPX Missing Elevation | Takeoff prior to GNSS lock (`OsdHeight == 0`, geoid unavailable) | Emit takeoff ground reference barometric elevation or zero; do not emit NaN or empty `<ele></ele>`. |
484: | 15 | GeoJSON RFC 7946 CRS | Attempting to specify custom CRS projection (e.g. UTM or EPSG:3857) | RFC 7946 § 4 strictly deprecates the `crs` member. GeoJSON MUST strictly use WGS84 CRS84 (`[lon, lat, alt]`). |
485: | 16 | Time Window Filter | `--start` time is greater than `--end` time (e.g. `--start 50 --end 20`) | Exporter rejects time window with typed error `ExportError::InvalidTimeWindow` and aborts. |
486: | 17 | Time Window Filter | `--start` is greater than flight duration (e.g. `--start 9999`) | Emits warning, generates empty file with valid headers/schema, and exits cleanly. |
487: | 18 | Decimation Landmark Drop | Aggressive decimation (`--rate 0.1`, 1 point per 10s) drops motor startup / RTH trigger | Pinned landmarks must bypass decimation bins. A critical event record must be inserted regardless of bin occupancy. |
488: | 19 | Blackbox .DAT Ingestion | Exporting blackbox `.DAT` logs containing no mobile app warnings or GPS details | Export routines must gracefully populate missing mobile fields with defaults or omit optional columns without panicking. |
489: | 20 | Dual Battery Ingestion | Ingesting enterprise logs from Matrice 300 RTK with two active battery packs | CSV exporter must dynamically expand column headers from `BATTERY.*` to include `BATTERY2.*` to prevent truncation of Battery 2 data. |
490: | 21 | XML Entity Injection | Aircraft name or warning message contains unescaped `&`, `<`, or `>` | XML parsers fail with fatal XML syntax errors unless special characters are escaped (`&`, `<`, `>`) or enclosed in CDATA. |
